intent: Makes the documented npx quick start actually run. Every invocation in README.md (8 of them) and in downstream contributor docs has the shape `npx -y "git+https://github.com/amos-labs/plumbline#v0.7.2" <cmd>`. npx resolves `<spec> <args>` to the bin entry whose NAME MATCHES THE PACKAGE NAME. This package is named `plumbline`, but its bin map declared only `plumb` and `proofgate` — so no bin matched, npx could not choose one, and the command exited 0 having done nothing: no output, no error, exit code 0. That is the worst failure mode a quick start can have, because it is indistinguishable from success. FOUND IN THE FIELD, not in review: while following the documented receipt flow in the cuspr repo on npm 10.8.2 / Node 20, every npx form produced zero bytes on both stdout and stderr. The downstream cost was concrete — cuspr contributors had given up on the CLI and were hand-computing diff_sha256 with a bare `git diff | shasum`, which cannot reproduce the hermetic binding introduced in v0.7.1. That produced four consecutive REWORK verdicts and re-stamp commits on cuspr PRs #416-#419, plus a wrong root-cause diagnosis (CI base resolution under a shallow fetch) that survived until someone ran `plumb diff-hash` from a local checkout — at which point the CLI printed both the hermetic and legacy hashes and named the divergence in plain text. The tool was right and self-diagnosing all along; nobody could reach it. THE FIX: add `plumbline` to the bin map, keeping `plumb` (short ergonomic alias, used for local checkouts) and `proofgate` (pre-rename name still baked into older repos' scripts) so no existing caller breaks. Adds src/test/npx-bin-name.test.ts pinning the invariant that the package name is always a bin key, plus that both historical aliases survive and every bin points at dist/index.js. NOTE FOR THE RELEASE: this only reaches users once tagged — downstream pins a version in the npx spec and in action.yml, so v0.7.2 stays broken for them until a v0.7.3 exists. Tagging is deliberately left to the maintainer rather than done here.

Cannot run until a v0.7.3 tag exists — the npx spec pins a tag, so this is only observable after release. Baseline recorded for comparison: on npm 10.8.2 / Node 20 the v0.7.2 spec returns 0 bytes on stdout AND stderr with exit 0, for the bare form, the explicit-command form, and the `-p <spec> plumb <cmd>` form alike, while `git ls-remote` resolves the tag fine and `node <checkout>/dist/index.js diff-hash` works correctly — isolating bin resolution rather than fetch or the CLI itself.

result_summary: The documented npx quick start has been a silent no-op: package `plumbline` had bins `plumb` and `proofgate` but none matching the package name, so `npx -y <spec> <cmd>` could not resolve a binary and exited 0 with no output. Adding a `plumbline` bin fixes all 8 README invocations at once; the two existing aliases are kept so nothing that already worked breaks. This was not cosmetic — cuspr contributors, unable to reach the CLI, fell back to a bare `git diff | shasum` that cannot reproduce the hermetic v0.7.1 binding, which cost four re-stamp commits across PRs #416-#419 and a wrong root-cause diagnosis that only collapsed once the CLI was run from a local checkout and printed the hermetic-vs-legacy divergence itself. New test pins the package-name-is-a-bin-key invariant and was verified to fail without the fix. 328/328 tests pass. Needs a v0.7.3 tag to reach users, since downstream pins the version in both the npx spec and action.yml.
